result.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
result.comment: Accepted at the Interpretability for Discovery (Interp4Discovery) Workshop at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
result.summary: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. We port GLP to ESM-2 activations (UniRef50) and evaluate it at two host scales (ESM-2-8M and -650M), both as a lens for protein representations and as a prior for editing them. Generation quality scales smoothly with depth and compute. As a lens, single GLP "meta-neurons" are the strongest probes of discrete Swiss-Prot concepts at both hosts, beating InterPLM's released SAE features, and lead on continuous properties at 8M though not at 650M; falsification tests show this is mostly concentration, not new information. As an editing prior, the on-manifold correction makes DiffMean steering of three biochemical properties effective and restores on-manifoldness, but only in isolation: re-embedding the sequences actually produced after several rounds of decoding, the structural plausibility is compromised. This is mainly reproduced in additional SAE-based clamping structural steering experiments, where only Helix motif succeeds. The naturalness failure is traced to the rewriting coverage and the decoder rather than the prior, highlighting what the method must clear before it can serve for both discovery-by-editing and discovery-by-exploration. Trained GLPs are released on huggingface.co/collections/HPAI-BSC/glprot.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把扩散式「生成潜先验」（GLP）迁移到 ESM-2 激活上，既用作探测离散概念与连续属性的解释透镜，也用作 on-manifold 校正与 DiffMean steering 的编辑先验，并发现多轮解码后序列结构合理性会劣化。
AI.relevance_reason: 对冻结模型激活分布建模并做流形内校正与状态编辑，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的干预、真实性与「编辑后能否解码回有效证据」提供可核查的方法线索，但对象是蛋白质序列，与视觉推理相距较远。
